findings.what: Promotion deletes the attempt workspace before clearing the interrupted-promotion marker, so a reachable final-cleanup interruption produces a repair-required result that points to a workspace that no longer exists.
findings.why: `promote_workspace` durably writes completed state, calls `discard_workspace(workspace)`, and only then unlinks `.anomaly/promotion.json`. A process stop between those calls, or failure of the final unlink, leaves startup-visible interruption evidence after the promised inspection workspace has already been destroyed. This violates AC4 and the installed manual-repair contract. The new marker tests fabricate a marker beside an intact workspace instead of exercising this producer ordering. Add a deterministic producer-boundary test, then clear the marker before discarding the workspace so any surviving marker implies the workspace is still retained.

findings.what: The change deletes the deterministic interrupted-attempt reconciliation test even though the corresponding public restart behavior remains in production.
findings.why: `test_restart_reconciles_a_hard_exit_after_the_attempt_count_write` was removed, but `run_attempts` still calls unchanged `_reconcile_interrupted_attempt` at `src/anomaly/attempts.py:121`, which converts an active attempt lacking failure evidence into a bounded recorded failure before retrying. The remaining resume tests cover completed-state idempotency, event-store failure, or manually fabricated promotion markers; none covers this retained consumer-observable transition. Deleting its test without deleting the behavior violates the testing skill's removal/redundancy rule and leaves AC5's ordinary restart/resume contract under-tested. Restore or rewrite the deterministic failpoint test without asserting automatic promotion rollback.
